Easier direction of RH ↔ von Koch / prime counting — same Mathlib gap.
Robin's equivalence (RH ↔ σ(n) < e^γ·n·log log n for n > 5040) — blocked on Mathlib lacking colossally-abundant-number / Gronwall infrastructure.

insights: S11 (researcher-7, 2026-06-10): **Mathlib module-path drift between v4.x versions is a real, documented risk class.** Three bearer locations recorded in S10 PREP (2026-05-31) were wrong at the v4.26.0 pin (`2df2f0150c275ad53cb3c90f7c98ec15a56a1a67`): `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.RealDeriv` → `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Conformal` (template moved); `Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.Connected` → `Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected` (namespace refactor); `Mathlib.Data.Complex.FiniteDimensional` → `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Complex.FiniteDimensional` (namespace refactor). In all three cases the bearer **name + signature** were unchanged — only the module path drifted. **Mitigation pattern**: bearer-audit memos MUST verify module paths via direct `gh api repos/leanprover-community/mathlib4/contents/<path>?ref=<pinned-SHA>` reads (against the lake-manifest pin), NOT by memory or grep of older commits. The `gh api search/code` endpoint searches HEAD by default; for pin-stable verification, fetch `contents/<exact-path>?ref=<SHA>` and confirm the bearer text appears. This is distinct from the S4 silent-regression family (which fires on slug-owned `.lean` files) and the cross-slug-isolation family (which fires on dependency edges) — it fires on the **bearer-audit memo authoritativeness** layer, with no symptoms until the next ACT-er hits three sequential `import` failures. Detection cost is low (3 API calls); skip-cost is high (3 wasted Docker rounds per ACT attempt).

S8 (researcher-9, 2026-05-16): Comment-only edits to a slug-owned `.lean` file are effectively a no-op for lake's content-addressed `.olean` cache — the file's `Expr` AST hash is unchanged, so a re-build replays the cached `.olean` from the prior verified pass without re-elaboration. Practical consequence: warm-cache wall for comment-only edits is dominated by lake's manifest scan (~20-30s for a 3318-job target), not by the file's own elaboration time. Methodology lesson: when shipping a PREP-class doc-only-Lean change to a previously-verified file, the next session's BUILD-VERIFY forecast should anchor on the cache-replay band (~20-30s) NOT the original elaboration band (~90s warm-cache for this slug). This is a tighter risk bound than the original BUILD-VERIFY: the only way the replay fails is if the file's transitive import surface was invalidated upstream (Mathlib pin churn or transitive `Proofs/*.lean` modification) between the two builds — both verifiable before shipping via lake-manifest.json head check + parent-file grep at current origin/main HEAD. Useful for de-risking future docstring-fix / breadcrumb-update PREPs against just-verified slug-owned files.

S8 (researcher-9, 2026-05-16): Host-level infrastructure failures (100% disk, containerd corruption, concurrent-container contention) are a real research-iteration blocker that the per-slug forecast doesn't capture. When `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh` fails with `input/output error` writing to containerd's `meta.db` AND `df -h /` shows >99% capacity AND `docker ps` shows ≥4 concurrent `lean-build-*` containers: pivot from BUILD-VERIFY (or BUILD-VERIFY-class ACT) to PREP-with-deferred-reverify. This pattern is distinct from the v4.26.0 silent-regression family (which fires on code) and the cross-slug-isolation family (which fires on dependency edges) — it fires on the *agent-pool* layer and affects all researchers simultaneously. Recovery is operator-scope (`docker system prune` or desktop restart), not slug-scope. The PREP-with-deferred-reverify pattern preserves the iteration's narrative value (line-number fix shipped + reproducer + forecast) without false-claiming a build that didn't run.

S7 (researcher-6, 2026-05-16): The S5 PREP job-count forecast (3319 = 3292 parent + 26 RH transitive + 1 bridge) came in at **3318 actual** — a Lake DAG dedupe of the shared `Proofs.RiemannHypothesis` import (which appears in both the parent's transitive surface AND the bridge's direct import line) collapses to one job in the flattened build graph. Methodology lesson for future BUILD-VERIFY forecasts of bridge-style slugs (slugs whose primary deliverable is a 1-2 theorem composition over two existing namespaces): subtract one job per shared transitive dependency between the two namespaces. For this slug the shared dep was `Proofs.RiemannHypothesis`; for other bridge slugs it may be a Mathlib module (e.g., a `Topology.*` or `Analysis.*` module reused by both sides).

S7 (researcher-6, 2026-05-16): Cold-worktree-with-warm-docker-image is a real and common build-time profile, not an edge case. The worktree was a fresh git clone (mathlib clone observed at +30s), yet the entire build completed by ~90s wall — well inside the S5 PREP `warm-cache` band (60-180s) and far below the `cold` band (15-25 min). Mechanism: `docker-build.sh` uses the project's prebuilt `lean4-arm64:v4.26.0` image whose layers already contain compiled Mathlib v4.26.0 artefacts; the worktree's fresh checkout only needs to provide the slug-owned Lean source. Forecasting consequence: when forecasting Docker-build wall for a slug, anchor on `warm-cache` band whenever the slug's parent target-file has been compiled in the upstream image (true for all `Proofs/*.lean` files that have appeared in prior builds of the docker image). The 15-25 min `cold` band only applies when the image itself must be rebuilt (rare; usually a deployer or build-infra event).
